rule: FROZEN BEFORE THE SEQUENCE WAS RUN. HR-20. The six verbs each passed alone; nothing has strung them together, and every failure this week appeared AT A SEAM rather than inside a unit.
scope: one real sequence, headed, on a live READ-ONLY destination: navigate, read, click, read again, type, wait. Nothing that submits.

criteria.must: a ref taken BEFORE an action still resolves to the same element after an action that did not disturb it. This is the whole premise of read_page and has never been tested across an action.
a ref to an element the DOM removed REFUSES with ELEMENT_GONE. It must never resolve to a different element and never report success.
a ref taken before a NAVIGATION must not silently address a node in the new document. Whatever it does, it must not be a wrong click reported as a right one.
the report alone says what was done, to what, in what order, what was refused and why — without needing the turns. Same bet as the enquiry runner.
no typed value appears anywhere in the report
no coordinates appear anywhere in the report
the sequence STOPS at the first refusal with a named reason. It does not continue, does not retry, and does NOT stop by timing out.

a refusal that is knowable without waiting (origin not in order, credential field, element gone) is reported in well under the action timeout — a stop that arrives as a timeout is indistinguishable from a hang

acceptanceBar: S1-S8 all demonstrated in ONE live headed run against a real page, with the report printed in full so it can be judged on its own.
notInScope: the offline/desktop half. Separate estimate, separate evidence, separate codebase.
